id: The Men That Don't Fit In

prompts.L3:
Please expand the following bullet points into a complete, well-structured text:

- Some people are restless by nature and cannot settle, causing pain to loved ones as they wander the world.
- Although they may be strong, brave, and capable, their constant desire for novelty prevents them from staying on a steady path.
- They repeatedly believe the next change will help them find their purpose, but each new move becomes another mistake.
- The poem contrasts their fitful energy with the quiet persistence of steady people, who ultimately succeed in life.
- In the end, the restless wanderer realizes too late that he has wasted his chances and was never suited to fit in.
prompts.L4:
Please expand the following two-sentence summary into a complete text:

The poem explores restless people who cannot settle into ordinary life, using vivid imagery of wandering, changing paths, and chasing novelty to portray their inability to commit. It concludes that despite their strength and potential, their lack of persistence leads to failure, emphasizing that steady perseverance—not restless brilliance—wins life’s race.

Keywords: There, And, They

outputs.L1:
There is a race of men who do not fit in,  
A race that cannot remain still;  
They break the hearts of kith and kin,  
And roam the world at will.  

They range across the fields and rove the seas,  
They climb the mountain’s crest;  
Theirs is the curse of gypsy blood,  
And they do not know how to rest.  

If only they went straight, they might go far;  
They are strong and brave and true.  
Yet they are always weary of things as they are,  
And long for the strange and new.  

They say, “Could I but find my proper groove,  
What a deep mark I would make!”  
So they chop and change, and every fresh move  
Becomes only a fresh mistake.  

And each forgets, as he strips and runs  
With a brilliant, fitful pace,  
That it is the steady, quiet, plodding ones  
Who win the lifelong race.  

And each forgets that his youth has fled,  
Forgets that his prime is past,  
Until he stands one day, with a hope that is dead,  
In the glare of the truth at last.  

He has failed—he has failed; he has missed his chance;  
He has only done things by half.  
Life has been a jolly good joke on him,  
And now is the time to laugh.  

Ha, ha! He is one of the Legion Lost;  
He was never meant to win.  
He is a rolling stone, and it is bred in the bone;  
He is a man who will not fit in.
outputs.L2:
There are people who never seem to belong anywhere,  
people who are unable to remain in one place.  
They cause pain to family and friends,  
then wander wherever the world allows.  
They cross open country, travel over water,  
and scale the tops of mountains.  
Restlessness is in their blood like a curse,  
and peace is something they cannot understand.

If they chose one clear path, they could achieve a great deal.  
They have courage, strength, and honesty.  
Yet ordinary life soon wearies them,  
and they constantly long for what is unfamiliar and different.  
They tell themselves, “If only I could discover the right place for me,  
I would leave a powerful impression there.”  
But they keep altering their plans, shifting direction again and again,  
and every new start becomes another wrong turn.

Each one forgets, as he rushes forward in bursts of bright energy,  
that it is the patient, steady, persistent people  
who succeed over the long course of life.  
He also forgets that his youth is gone,  
and that his best years have slipped behind him,  
until one day he is forced to face the truth,  
standing with his hopes extinguished.

He has fallen short; he has failed.  
His opportunity passed him by.  
He has never fully completed what he began.  
Life has played a grand joke on him,  
and now there is nothing left to do but laugh.  
Ha, ha! He belongs among the lost and defeated;  
victory was never really meant for him.  
He is a born wanderer, restless to the core—  
a man who can never fit in.
outputs.L3:
Some people seem to be born restless. They cannot remain in one place, follow one path, or accept the ordinary limits of a settled life. Their uneasiness drives them from home to home, from one ambition to another, and from one dream to the next. Yet this wandering does not affect them alone. Those who love them often suffer most, watching helplessly as they leave behind comfort, loyalty, and responsibility in search of something they cannot clearly name.

These people may possess many admirable qualities. They may be strong, courageous, intelligent, and capable of great effort. However, their gifts are weakened by their constant craving for novelty. Instead of using their abilities patiently and steadily, they are always tempted by the possibility of change. A new place, a new occupation, or a new adventure seems to promise a fuller life. Because of this, they are unable to remain on a firm and consistent path long enough to build anything lasting.

Again and again, the restless person convinces himself that the next change will be the right one. He believes that one more journey, one more decision, or one more fresh beginning will finally reveal his true purpose. But each move only leads to another disappointment. What first appears to be an opportunity becomes another error, and what seems like freedom turns into confusion. Instead of moving closer to meaning, he drifts farther away from it.

The poem contrasts this fitful, unsettled energy with the quiet persistence of steadier people. These people may appear less exciting or less daring, but they possess the patience to continue. They accept routine, endure difficulty, and work consistently toward their goals. Over time, their calm determination brings success. While the wanderer is always beginning again, they are slowly building a life.

In the end, the restless wanderer comes to understand the truth too late. He sees that his constant searching has cost him his opportunities, his relationships, and his peace. He realizes that he was never able to fit into the stable world around him, yet his refusal to settle has not brought him freedom either. His life becomes a sad example of wasted promise: a person gifted with strength and courage, but unable to use them wisely because he could never stay still long enough to belong.
outputs.L4:
The poem presents a vivid portrait of restless people who are unable to settle into the ordinary routines and responsibilities of life. These individuals are full of energy, imagination, and desire, but they are constantly dissatisfied with whatever path they choose. Instead of remaining faithful to one purpose, they wander from place to place and from idea to idea, always searching for something newer, brighter, or more exciting. The imagery of shifting roads, changing directions, and endless movement suggests a life without stability. Such people are drawn by novelty and possibility, but they lack the patience to remain with one task long enough to complete it.

Through this portrayal, the poem shows that restlessness can be both attractive and destructive. The restless person may seem strong, gifted, and full of promise, yet that promise is wasted when it is not guided by discipline. Because they cannot commit themselves to steady effort, they fail to turn their abilities into lasting achievement. Their lives become a series of beginnings without endings, attempts without fulfillment, and dreams without results.

In the end, the poem suggests that success in life does not belong merely to the most brilliant or energetic people. It belongs to those who can endure, persist, and continue working even when the excitement has faded. Strength and talent are valuable, but without perseverance they are incomplete. The poem’s final message is that life’s race is won not by restless brilliance, but by steady, faithful determination.
outputs.L5:
There are moments in life when everything feels uncertain, and people must decide how to move forward. They may not always know the right path, but each step teaches them something new.

And even when challenges appear, hope can remain. There is strength in patience, courage in kindness, and wisdom in learning from mistakes. They discover that progress does not always happen quickly, but it happens when they keep trying.

Robert W. Service’s “The Men That Don’t Fit In” is in the public domain.

## The Men That Don’t Fit In

There’s a race of men that don’t fit in,  
A race that can’t stay still;  
So they break the hearts of kith and kin,  
And they roam the world at will.  
They range the field and they rove the flood,  
And they climb the mountain’s crest;  
Theirs is the curse of the gypsy blood,  
And they don’t know how to rest.

If they just went straight they might go far—  
They are strong, and brave, and true;  
But they’re always tired of the things that are,  
And they want the strange and new.  
They say: “Could I find my proper groove,  
What a deep mark I would make!”  
So they keep on going and never stop,  
And they never find their place.

He has failed, he has failed; he has missed his chance;  
He has just done things by half.  
Life’s been a jolly good joke on him,  
And now is the time to laugh.  
Ha, ha! He is one of the Legion Lost;  
He was never meant to win;  
He’s a rolling stone, and it’s bred in the bone;  
He’s a man who won’t fit in.
